title: How Many Days Do You Need to Climb Kilimanjaro?
excerpt: The number of days you spend on Kilimanjaro affects your chance of reaching the top more than almost anything else. Here is how to decide.
body:
The most common question we get about Kilimanjaro is how many days it takes. The honest answer: more than you would like, and fewer than you fear.

## The minimum

Technically you can climb Kilimanjaro in five days on the Marangu Route. We do not recommend it. Going from around 1,800 m to 5,895 m in four days gives your body very little time to adapt, and many people turn back with altitude symptoms.

## Our recommendation

- **7 days** on Machame or Rongai.
- **8 days** on Lemosho, our most common advice.
- **9 days** on the Northern Circuit for the best acclimatisation.

## Why extra days help

At higher altitude there is less oxygen in every breath. Your body adapts by producing more red blood cells and changing your breathing, but that takes days. Each extra night between 3,500 and 4,600 m makes the final climb more manageable.

## What about fitness?

Fitness helps you enjoy the climb, but it does not protect you from altitude sickness. Very fit people who climb too fast can get sick too. That is why days on the mountain matter more than marathon times.

## Add time before and after

Plan one night in Moshi or Arusha before the climb to recover from your flight, and one after. Many people add a [safari](/blog/kilimanjaro-and-safari-combined/) or a few days on [Zanzibar](/blog/kilimanjaro-and-zanzibar/).

## In short

If you can, choose eight days. If you have seven, choose a route with a good climb-high-sleep-low profile. [Plan your climb with us](/travel-proposal/).
